title: Flattening by an admissible blowup (Raynaud--Gruson)
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let $U\subseteq T$ be a quasi-compact open subscheme, and let $g:W\to T$ be a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] which is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] and whose restriction $g^{-1}(U)\to U$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Then there is a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ of finite type with $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$ (a $U$-admissible blowup centre [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]) such that, writing $\pi:T'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(T)\to T$ for its blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup], the strict transform $W'\subseteq W\times_TT'$ of $W$ [def-nagata-strict-transform], namely the scheme-theoretic closure in $W\times_TT'$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] of the open subscheme lying over $T\setminus V(\mathcal I)$, is flat over $T'$ and of finite presentation over $T'$, that is, locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 081R, lemma-flat-after-blowing-up; strict transform as in literature/stacks-project/divisors.tex Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform. Cited by literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf, Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.4, Step 2 (Raynaud-Gruson 5.7.9).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flattening-ambient-module-preparation] to $g$ and $U$. It supplies a finite affine cover $W=\bigcup_i W_i$, closed immersions $j_i:W_i\hookrightarrow V_i$ with $V_i\to T$ quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation, and finite-type quasi-coherent modules $\mathcal F_i=(j_i)_*\mathcal O_{W_i}$ whose restrictions over $U$ are finitely presented and flat over $U$.

For each $i$, apply [lem-trf-flattening-module-by-admissible-blowup] to $V_i\to T$, $\mathcal F_i$ and $U$. The base is qcqs, $U$ is quasi-compact, and step 1 supplies all four ambient and module hypotheses. Obtain a finite-type quasi-coherent centre $\mathcal I_i$, equal to the unit ideal on $U$, with blowup $b_i:T_i\to T$ such that $\mathcal F_i^{b_i}$ is flat over $T_i$ and finitely presented over $V_i\times_T T_i$.

Apply [lem-trf-flattening-closed-immersion-transfer] to $p:V_i\to T$, $j_i$ and $\mathcal I_i$. Its comparison identifies $\mathcal F_i^{b_i}$ with the pushed structure sheaf of the scheme strict transform $W_i^{(i)}$, for the complement of $V(\mathcal I_i)$. The flatness and finite presentation obtained in step 2 therefore give flatness and local finite presentation of $W_i^{(i)}\to T_i$.

Apply [lem-trf-flattening-finite-cover-common-blowup] to this finite affine cover and the ideals $\mathcal I_i$. Its hypothesis on each individual strict transform is step 3, and $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by the assumptions. It gives the product centre $\mathcal I=\prod_i\mathcal I_i$, a $U$-admissible blowup $T^b\to T$, and flatness, local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of the strict transform of $W$ for that centre. These are exactly the claimed flatness and finite presentation, with the strict transform taken over $T\setminus V(\mathcal I)$.
